Items (GRAMMAR-NEEDS.md has the status and file refs at 7c3ff0a):
- G39 all-events term and main + slopes pairing: hrf(...) requires a variable (FormulaParser.scala:424); hrf(x, modulators(...)) yields slope columns only (a ScalaFIM scenario test confirms the column count; found in critiques/m4b-methods.md). Need an all-events form (e.g. hrf(1, …)) and an explicit pairing (e.g. include_main) so a modulated term is one model statement.
- G32 kernel-level unit-peak normalization: formula normalize = TRUE divides each column by its own maximum (EventModelBuilder.scala:1138–1144), so divisors differ by column and run (e.g. sample 1.93 vs probe 1.00; gain×loss 267 vs 288 across runs). The studio uses peak-normalized kernels (HrfNormalization.UnitPeak exists on HrfSpec but is not reachable from the formula). Raw spmg1 peaks ≈ 0.175, so SE/σ differ ≈ 5.7×.
- G1 / G34 spans: FIR span (Hrfs.fir(nBasis) uses the default span); B-spline span (studio 20 s, default 24 s).
- G2 serial orthogonalization in the formula (exists only as BuildOptions/ModelBuildSpec.orthogonalization).
- G3 / G20 product modulators of run-centred components inside modulators() (gain:loss with each factor centred within run before the product).
- G4 one slope shared across cells while the main effect is split.
- G9 / G30 derivative conventions: at 7c3ff0a spmg3's third function is the second time derivative; HEAD implements a true dispersion derivative. The studio uses SPM's temporal derivative as a 1-s finite difference and the dispersion derivative (h(d=1) − h(d=1.01))/0.01 (K_TD/BASES lines 398–404). Name the convention.
- G14 derivative-basis orthogonalization (spm_orth on the convolved columns, per cell and modulator stream; build() line 566) as a term option, default SPM-like for spmg2/3.
Durations (resolved, no change needed): the studio's integral convention equals ScalaFIM's default summate = TRUE (methods critic confirmed from Pulse.fromSummate/Regressor: impulse peak 1.000, 1 s 0.969, 2 s 1.781, 10 s 5.398).
Acceptance: each item parses, builds and round-trips through SF4; R parity fixtures where fmridesign has an equivalent; the five example studies' default formulas print with no proposed flags except intended ones.

Evidence bundle (durable, not in Git): /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/plsneuro-fixtures/model-studio-hillclimb-20261002 — start with README.md there (layout, reference-implementation line map, how to run the audits, verified numbers).
Reference implementation: /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/plsneuro-fixtures/model-studio-hillclimb-20261002/out/m7b/index.html (single inline script; line numbers below refer to it). It is a design mock on synthetic data: use it as a behavioural specification and a source of fixtures, not as validated science.
Design spec and consumer plan (PLS Neuro, branch studio/model-authoring-hillclimb at d47c988, worktree /private/tmp/plsneuro-model-studio): docs/plans/2026-10-02-model-studio-spec.md (invariants I1–I13 in section 3), docs/plans/2026-10-02-model-studio-native-plan.md. Grammar ledger with ScalaFIM file refs: /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/plsneuro-fixtures/model-studio-hillclimb-20261002/GRAMMAR-NEEDS.md.
Example studies for fixtures: STUDIES (line 424): block localizer (TR 2, N 180), mixed gambles (N 240; gain, loss, gain×loss), delayed match-to-sample (N 210; sample/delay/probe/errors phases; accuracy), stop signal (N 200; FIR 10×2 s; rt n/a for successful stops, ssd n/a for go), category × attention (N 240; 12 cells × canonical+temporal+dispersion; 24 motion). Runs use seeds 11 and 29; motion from motionSet (418); FD/censoring and confounds in regenMotion (499).
